newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish ministry sees private consumption recovery.
newsitem.headline: Spanish ministry sees private consumption recovery.

text.p: The Spanish Economy Ministry said on Thursday private consumption was showing its first signs of a more intense recovery, which should help the goverment reach its GDP growth goals of 2.3 percent in 1996 and 3.0 percent in 1997.

"Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato said that private consumption is showing the first signs of a more intense recovery which will make it possible to reach the growth objectives of 2.3 percent in 1996 and of three percent in 1997," the Ministry said in a statement.

"The revival of private consumption can be detected in the growth of industrial goods production, large store sales, VAT receipts, imports of consumer goods and car registrations," Rato said, according to the statement.
